A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPPO research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Retained content can be matched despite additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments, ablations, robustness analyses, and physical robot evaluations with 20 trials per method.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and hardware results and adds experiments comparing demonstration-augmented RL methods, including Franka Kitchen evaluations.

M1.justification: The two-layer diffusion MDP, PPO update, advantage estimator, partial denoising fine-tuning, DDIM option, and noise clipping remain unchanged. The prediction/execution horizon distinction clarifies existing operation; revised training configurations do not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds Franka Kitchen with Complete, Partial, and Mixed demonstration datasets, extending evaluation to countertop tasks with varying demonstration completeness. Figure 6 also adds Proficient-Human data for ROBOMIMIC Can and Square alongside Multi-Human data. Earlier benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New Section 5.2 and Figure 6 evaluate RLPD, Cal-QL, and IBRL against DPPO on HalfCheetah, Franka Kitchen, and ROBOMIMIC. These substantially broaden the comparator set beyond the diffusion-based algorithms and PPO-trained policy parameterizations evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The hyperparameter tables substantially revise learning rates, replay ratios, buffers, and batch sizes. For example, IDQL replay ratios change from 16 to 128, and the diffusion-algorithm comparison changes DPPO's Gym batch size from 5,000 to 50,000 and fine-tuned denoising steps from 20 to 10. New Kitchen comparisons use four-step actions and 40 environments for DPPO versus single-step actions and one environment for baselines. These reported changes do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The existing Appendix B ablations and Section 6 robustness plots are retained. New qualitative sensitivity findings include testing one-step versus four-step actions for RLPD, Cal-QL, and IBRL in Appendix D.6, and the effect of smaller DPPO batches on ROBOMIMIC sample efficiency in Appendix D.5.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly suppresses QSM's Hopper uncertainty band in Figure 5; v2 displays that shading and removes the suppression note. Existing five-seed Gym, three-seed ROBOMIMIC, and 20-trial hardware reporting remains unchanged; the new comparisons largely follow the existing seed-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 5 replaces learning curves under revised configurations, with Section 5.1 now identifying DIPO rather than DAWR as competitive in Gym and IDQL as strong in several ROBOMIMIC tasks. QSM's Hopper iteration time changes from 64.4 to 9.6 seconds in Table A1. New Figure 6 reports additional comparisons, including stronger off-policy sample efficiency in HalfCheetah and stronger DPPO final success on Can and Square. These are revised or additional results, not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The MDP construction, policy-gradient derivation, PPO definition, and denoising-discounted advantage remain mathematically unchanged. Action-horizon notation and descriptions of established comparator losses add explanation without new theoretical reasoning, assumptions, proofs, or guarantees.

C1.justification: Contribution 2 expands the comparative claim to demonstration-augmented RL and qualifies final-performance superiority with 'often.' The abstract's central message, DPPO contribution, mechanism claims, and principal hardware and Transport claims remain stable.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies lower sample efficiency than off-policy methods as DPPO's main limitation and distinguishes this from its parallelized wall-clock advantage. Section 5.2 and Appendix D.6 add explanations of incomplete-demonstration failures, sensitivity to pre-training mode coverage, and seed variability relative to Cal-QL. These substantially extend v1's existing discussion of structured exploration and coverage limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds implementation descriptions and settings for the new baselines and Kitchen experiments, plus a DPPO batch-size explanation. Hardware state estimation expands from a brief filtering description to camera placement, rejection thresholds, smoothing, pose caching, normalization, and debugging guidance. These are newly documented details, without evidence that the retained hardware evaluation changed. Some new Table A8 cells remain malformed or ambiguous.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially broadens positioning around demonstration-augmented RL, residual policies, offline-data replay, and offline-to-online learning. Section 2 and Appendix A.2 are correspondingly expanded, with 17 additional references and the earlier cited works retained.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a comparison subsection and several appendix subsections, clarifies prediction versus execution horizons, and expands hardware explanations into organized points. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order remain intact; there is no wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multipanel Figure 6, revises Figure 5's plotted ranges, and expands several tables. The former Tables A7–A8 are consolidated into Table A7, while v2's Table A8 presents new baseline settings. Most other figures retain their graphics and are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important comparison gap by testing broader demonstration-augmented RL competitors and examining incomplete demonstrations. It also makes sample-efficiency limitations explicit and substantially improves hardware reproducibility information. Revised configurations prevent interpreting changed scores as pure performance gains, and Table A8 has ambiguities, but the broader evidence and clearer applicability boundaries provide a substantial net improvement.
